what_its_for: Cyclobenzaprine is a muscle relaxer used for short-term relief of muscle spasms, stiffness, and pain caused by muscle injuries or strains. It works by blocking nerve signals in your brain that cause muscles to tighten up. It is usually used along with rest and physical therapy.
how_to_take: Take cyclobenzaprine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. For the extended-release capsule (Amrix), swallow it whole and do not open or crush it. Try to take it at the same time each day. Do not take it for longer than 2 to 3 weeks unless your doctor says so.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 5 mg taken 3 times a day. Your doctor may increase this to 10 mg taken 3 times a day if needed. For the extended-release capsule, it is usually 15 mg once daily, and can be increased to 30 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cyclobenzaprine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cyclobenzaprine — it can make drowsiness and dizziness much worse and can be dangerous. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything requiring you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medications, narcotic pain medicines, or antihistamines, unless your doctor approves. Avoid standing up too quickly, as this can cause dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a fast or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of an allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness or fainting, confusion or unusual thoughts, difficulty urinating, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), or seizures. Also call your doctor if your muscle pain and spasms are not improving after a few days.
when_it_works: Cyclobenzaprine usually starts to relieve muscle spasms within 1 to 3 days of starting treatment. You may notice some improvement in pain and stiffness within the first few hours after taking it. Most people feel significant relief within the first week. Remember, this medication works best when combined with rest and physical therapy.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Cyclobenzaprine is generally NOT recommended for older adults because it can cause serious side effects like confusion, falls, dizziness, and heart rhythm problems. Talk to your doctor about safer alternatives. Pregnancy: The safety of this medication during pregnancy is not well established. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if cyclobenzaprine passes into breast milk. Check with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medication is not approved for use in children under 15 years of age. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may need to lower your dose or choose a different medication.
